text:
sam: FYI onboarding crux-13B into the eval harness — hitting a weird tokenizer+collate interaction when prompts include emoji with trailing punctuation. Example that reproduces locally: 'Nice work! 🎉' seems to expand token count and shift KV alignment, causing collate to pad incorrectly.
jess: can you paste the exact prompt and the tokenizer output you see?
sam: sure — quick paste:```prompt = \"Nice work! 🎉\" tokens = tokenizer.encode(prompt) # crux-tokenizer v0.2.1 print(tokens) -> [502, 134, 12, 0, 4096, 4097] # mock ids showing extra tokens for emoji+VS```
kai: we saw something similar with nova2 where U+FE0F (variation selector) and ZWJ sequences split into multiple sub-tokens. are these emojis coming from user text or generated templates?
sam: coming from our chat templates (some celebratory lines). the issue is that some emoji sequences include U+FE0F or ZWJ and end up as multiple tokens. the eval runner's collate assumes token counts won't change relative to raw char heuristics, so the padding length is computed wrong. result is either mismatched kv cache shapes or subtle logits misalignment.
marta: is CI failing because of this? which test is blowing up?
sam: integration/evals/chat_template_padding_test fails intermittently. excerpt from logs: ```ValueError: mismatched kv cache shapes: expected (batch=8, seq=1024) got (batch=8, seq=1026) at runner.collate()```
ryan: that can cause OOMs on 2x batches. also inflates token accounting for hosted usage if we don't normalize.
evalbot: Auto-run: crux-13B (4-bit quant) — emoji-heavy chat templates show +0.8 BLEU drop vs baseline; token count per prompt +10% on average. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/crux/1234 (internal).
jess: proposed fixes: 1) add optional unicode normalization/tokenizer shim (NFKC or strip variation selectors) in eval harness per-model config, 2) change collate to compute pad lengths from tokenized sequences (safe canonicalization), 3) add regression tests with emoji+ZWJ fuzz cases.
sam: i'll prototype a normalization shim that runs pre-tokenize and adds an opt-in flag in model_config: `normalize_unicode: "nfkc"` or `strip_variation_selectors: true`. prototype snippet:```def normalize_input(s): import unicodedata; s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s) s = re.sub(r"\uFE0F", '', s) return s```
kai: also consider a canonicalizer that maps emoji to shortcodes for evals (emoji -> :party_popper:). that will make token counts deterministic across tokenizer variants.
marta: :thumbsup: keep this eval-only by default. we can't change serving tokens without product signoff. add a feature flag and document it in model onboarding checklist.
sam: agreed — eval-only opt-in flag. i'll open a PR with the shim, update the collate logic to use token lengths, and add fuzz tests for ZWJ/FE0F sequences. linking issue: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/issues/567
ryan: heads-up: if this leaks into Dedicated serving configs, it could affect billing and latency metrics; loop in infra if you plan a deploy.
jess: assigning review to kai + marta. if CI passes we'll merge behind a feature flag. can someone add a quick e2e that runs on small sample templates in the eval CI?
sam: will do. pinging @eng-oncall if CI flakes after the change. PR coming in a few hours.
jess: thanks — useful catch.
kai: thanks — happy to review the normalization edge cases.
ryan: adding a note to the onboarding doc to watch for emoji-induced token inflation.
marta: also add a dashboard alert rule: sudden avg tokens/prompt > 20% for a model -> trigger.
end of thread
